# `scope_fine_move`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Apply per-axis fine-move values and poll for stop with a timeout.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (native handler, 64-bit build) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0x7f850 (64-bit build); axis command helper speedMoveAxisCmd @0x68870 (rate command, timed-move command, 1440 clamp); wait for stop WaitScopeStop @0x68d10; formatter sites @0x7fa80 (210). Firmware 9.75 (64-bit build): handler @0x81030 (same instruction structure, relocated references); helper rate path @0x6a10c-0x6a3a4; wait @0x6a5dc-0x6a654 |

Firmware 9.31 and 9.75 (64-bit builds; READ). Requires a connected mount that reports motion support. The first two elements of the speed array supply the x/y values. If the coordinate read succeeds, the guider compensates x using the coordinate reported as altitude; a failed read skips compensation and continues. If the absolute coordinate exceeds 85 degrees, it is replaced with positive 85. When its degree cosine is greater than 0.1, the factor is the reciprocal rounded to single precision; otherwise the factor is 10. Only x is multiplied by it. When limit is enabled, comparable x/y values are then clamped to [-16, 16]. Each value is divided by the signed integer duration in double precision and narrowed to single precision. For finite divided rates, an absolute magnitude below the double-precision threshold 0.01 requests an axis abort instead of a rate or timed move; the abort's return value is not checked. A JSON value written as 0.01 is not guaranteed to reach the rate path, because the value is stored in single precision. For other finite rates, each magnitude is capped at 1440 and sent to the controller as its native rate value with two decimals, followed by a timed move, with no unit conversion in the guider; this is the same rate output that scope_speed_move uses. Anti-resonance snapping is disabled. The physical rate unit is unresolved (needs a device test). For axes that reach the timed move, backlash_comp true selects the :MTD command family; false uses the normal timed-move path, whose checked AM5 implementation uses :MT. Both receive the same duration integer. If neither axis operation reports failure to the handler, the guider polls movement status with a wait budget of duration plus 6 seconds when backlash_comp is true, or duration plus 2 seconds otherwise. It then replies with integer result 0, including after a stop-wait timeout. The reply does not establish an observed stop, physical completion, or acceptance of an abort request. Controller-side backlash behaviour is unresolved. The reviewed handler emits no completion event. The mount serial work runs in the request handler, not a worker (firmware 9.31 and 9.75, 64-bit and 32-bit, READ).

Side effects: Requests per-axis aborts, or rate and timed moves, then polls movement status with a timeout when the handler reaches its success path.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"scope_fine_move"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Firmware 9.31 and 9.75 (64-bit builds; READ). Parameters bind from a named object; a positional outer array supplies no bindings. Unknown members are ignored. Speed must be an array, not an object with x/y names. [READ] |
| `params.speed` | array<any> | yes | - | The first two elements supply x/y and must be numeric. At least two elements are required; later elements are ignored and may have any JSON type. Integers are read as signed 32-bit values; floating tokens are stored as single-precision values before widening for the calculation. Booleans and numeric strings are rejected. Missing, non-array or short speed, or invalid first-two values, take an error path that uses the thread-local error formatter (not a fixed 104/108). Values are native controller rate values; the physical unit is unresolved. Range: at least 2 item(s). [READ] |
| `params.limit` | boolean\|integer | no | true | Enables the comparable-value [-16, 16] clamp after any altitude compensation and before duration division. Boolean false and stored integer zero disable it; Boolean true and stored nonzero integers enable it. Integer storage is 32 bits. Missing or wrong-type values keep true; a floating token such as 0.0 does not disable the clamp. Disabling it does not disable altitude compensation or the separate per-axis rate cap of 1440. [READ] |
| `params.dur_sec` | integer | no | 1 | Defaults to 1 and accepts only an integer token, stored as a signed 32-bit value. Decimal or exponent tokens (such as 2.0), Booleans, strings, null, arrays and objects keep the default. Each axis value is divided by this duration in double precision, then narrowed to single precision, and the same integer is passed to the timed move. Zero and negative integers are kept without validation. Duration additions and the millisecond multiplication use 32-bit arithmetic. Device behaviour for zero, negative or overflowed durations is unresolved. [READ] |
| `params.backlash_comp` | boolean\|integer | no | false | Defaults to false. Boolean or stored 32-bit integer (zero is false, nonzero true); missing or wrong-type values keep false. For axes that reach the timed move, true selects the :MTD command family after a successful rate command; false selects the normal timed-move path (:MT in the checked AM5 implementation). The flag does not change the rate calculation or the duration. The stop-wait budget is duration plus 6 seconds for true and plus 2 seconds for false; a wait timeout still gives result 0. Physical backlash-compensation behaviour is unresolved. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 210 | The connected mount reports that motion is unsupported | `not supported` |
| 315 | The mount is absent or reports disconnected | `mount is not connected` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |

Missing or invalid speed, invalid first-two numeric values, and reported axis-operation failures format the current thread-local error, substituting 207 when it is zero; they have no fixed parameter-error code. A coordinate-read failure instead skips compensation and continues. A small-rate abort's return is not checked, and a stop-wait timeout still reaches result 0. Dispatcher codes (200, 100, 101, 103) are from firmware 9.31.

## Example

Request, minimal - speed only; values invented:

```json
{"id":90,"method":"scope_fine_move","params":{"speed":[4,-2]}}
```

Request, full - All optional members; values invented:

```json
{"id":91,"method":"scope_fine_move","params":{"speed":[8.5,0],"dur_sec":2,"limit":true,"backlash_comp":false}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_fine_move","result":0,"code":0,"id":90}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"scope_fine_move","error":"mount is not connected","code":315,"id":92}
```
